headline: Approved a Fern Street block party and prior minutes; crosswalk and Ridge Road study motions had no recorded outcome.
summary: The meeting covered crosswalk requests at Ridge Road and Hartford Turnpike, along with speeding and noise complaints near Ridge Road. Members approved the July and August minutes and a block party request at 32 Fern Street. The minutes do not record how the motions to refer the crosswalk requests and a Ridge Road traffic study ended.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 13 and August 10, 2026 meetings, unanimously.
Approved the block party request at 32 Fern Street for September 26, unanimously.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Traffic Authority Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, September 14, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center

2750 Dixwell Avenue

1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Chairman Willis called the Traffic Authority's regular meeting to order at 5:35 PM 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The Traffic Authority Clerk, Nancy Forvil, took a roll call. Commissioner's present: Willis, 
White, Zachery, Jones, Hampton and Ladore. 
 
Staff: Stehen White, Town Engineer and LTA. 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 LaShawn Jefferson 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
  a. Approval of minutes of the Traffic Authority's regular meetings on July 13th and 
August 10, 2026.  
  Commissioner Zachery made a motion to approve the regular meeting minutes of July 
13th and August 10, 2026.. Commissioner Jones seconded the motion. The vote was 
unanimous in favor. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 
 
  a. Janet Kazienko, 32 Fern Street - Block party request, between Wood & Mather, 9/26 
3:00PM-7:00PM, rain date 9/27  
  Commissioner Hampton made a motion to approve item 5a. Commissioner Jones 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  b. Tyrell Tyson, 103 Gorham Avenue — Accessible parking space approval request.
c. Glenbrook Avenue Residents - Speed hump request on Glenbrook Avenue. Motorists 
are speeding, hitting parked cars and utility poles. Residents are worried about the 
children who play in the neighborhood.  
  
 
6. REPORTS   
 
 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 There was no executive session. 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Robert B. Cochran, 687 Ridge Road— I would like to petition the city to install a 
crosswalk at this important intersection (Ridge Rd, Hartford Tpke, and Robinwood 
Rd). My wife and infant daughter and I live nearby and frequently cross this busy 
intersection on walks, and being forced to cross without any crosswalk (despite 
several sidewalks leading up to it!) creates a great deal of anxiety and is frankly 
unsafe. Given that the intersection lies in a scenic neighborhood, near a park, and 
along a route regularly used by the New Haven Bike Club, we frequently see other 
walkers, runners, and bicyclists also contending with the same problem.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8a to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
  b. Stephanie Profenna, 29 Myra Road—There’s a huge intersection by the firehouse on 
Hartford Turnpike and Ridge Road. With incoming traffic around the corner, it’s hard 
to cross the street from the dog park or children’s playground towards the firehouse. 
I’m often walking with my baby and dog in tow and don’t always feel safe crossing 
that road.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8b to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
  c. Eda Bozdemir, 137 Hepburn Road — Please add a crosswalk to this area for safety. 
(Ridge Rd, Hartford Turnpike, and Robinwood Rd)  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 8c to the traffic department to install 
crosswalk infrastructure when funding is available between Ridge Road and Hartford 
Turnpike. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Joan King I would like to know how we can improve the safety and extremely 
excessive auto noise on Ridge Rd and Hartford Tnpk, the streets surrounding the 
Coptic Church (formerly St Stephen’s) in our neighborhood.  I have complained to the 
police and nothing changes.  The cars are exceptionally loud, and they tear down 
Ridge and Hartford Turnpike at extremely dangerous high speeds throughout the day 
and late at night, especially Friday–Sunday.  The cars park and gather in the Coptic
Church lot.   We’re afraid there will be a tragic accident.   The traffic-calming islands 
do not stop them in the least.   Speed humps might be more effective, traffic cameras 
and police enforcement.   I’ve called the police numerous times. Nothing changes. 
This is ongoing, every week.  No one seems to care to do anything about it.  It has 
kept us up at nights and very distressed.  We are a quiet residential neighborhood.  I 
know this has been on the books for a long while now. It’s very discouraging. Is there 
anything more that can be done?  Speed humps? Speed Cameras and 
enforcement?  Is anyone else proposing these changes and improvements?  
  Commissioner White made a motion to refer item 9a to the traffic department for a 
traffic study on a portion of Ridge Road and review the weekend parking lot activity. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. 
  10. ADJOURNMENT  
 There being no further business to discuss, Commissioner Ladore made a motion to adjourn 
the Traffic Authority regular meeting. Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote 
was unanimous in favor. The meeting adjourned at 5:51 PM.

  a. Catherine Solomon, 25 Ranch Road — Block Party request for Saturday, July 18th 
on Ranch Road.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to move item 5a. to new business for a vote. 
Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
 
Commissioner Ladore made a motion to approve item 5a. in new business. 
Commissioner Hampton seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
6. REPORTS
Updates provided by LTA, Stephen White. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 (There was no executive session) 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Alyssa Krinsky, 104 Jesswig Drive — A section of High Meadow Rd between Ridge 
Rd and Hawley Rd was closed approximately 3 weeks ago, without notifying or 
consulting neighbors on adjacent streets in advance. We now experience people 
driving down Jesswig Dr and Hawley Rd at a high rate of speed coming from BOTH 
Ridge Rd and Hartford Tpk. I would request that traffic-calming measures be 
implemented on Jesswig Dr and Hawley Rd to ensure the safety of the residents in 
the area. Our recommendation would be the addition of a traffic light at one of the 
intersections with Ridge Rd (either High Meadow Rd or Jesswig Dr) to slow traffic 
and prevent accidents and speed bumps or speed humps to ensure those bypassing 
High Meadow Rd are unable to speed down these adjacent roads at high speeds.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to deny item 8a. Commissioner Hampton 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  b. Miguel Perez- Cabello — Stop Sign Request Corbin and Hepburn - "Stop signs are 
needed on Corbin Road at the corner with Hepburn Road. This corner is within a mile 
of Ridge Hill School. This is a school crossing guard spot. Many people, including 
children and seniors, cross this corner every day. Over the past few months, there 
have been several incidents in which cars traveling on Corbin Road have not 
stopped, almost causing an accident involving pedestrians or other cars. This corner 
is confusing for drivers and pedestrians because there are only two stop signs on 
Hepburn Road. Therefore, cars traveling on Corbin Road tend to drive through this 
corner without yielding. In addition, traffic from west to east on Corbin Road is 
downhill, which motivates drivers to go faster. The solution is simple: two stop signs 
need to be added on Corbin Road to ensure that there are four stop signs at this 
corner, so traffic from all points comes to a stop to prevent accidents involving other 
cars and pedestrians."  
  Item 8b. tabled. 
  c. Noemi Miranda-Foreman- Traffic Calming request Augur Street -– We have been 
experiencing too many cars speeding as well as driving up the wrong way since it is a 
one-way street. There are a lot of children that play out here and it's extremely 
dangerous when vehicles drive extremely fast. I have a security camera and 
sometimes cars drive so fast the camera barely picks it up. Having speed bumps will 
help control how fast cars are going and also help us be able to get out of our 
driveway safely without being hit by a speeding car. Please get speed bumps to 
control this issue on our street.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 8c. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner Zachery seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  d. Sean Cardwell, 2750 Dixwell Avenue — Request for traffic study to install stop signs 
along Evergreen Ave at the Dickerman Street intersection. The resident is requesting
a 4-way stop at the intersection because motorists constantly speed on Evergreen 
Ave.  
  Item 8d. tabled. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  a. Stephanie Weiner, 125 Mill Rock Road — I'm writing to add my voice to the chorus of 
neighbors in my area about three items: 1) I strongly support additional safety 
measures on Armory and Mill Rock, in particular cross walks, crossing tables, "slow 
down" language and other electronic signage, and automatic enforcement cameras. 
2) I hope we can hear an update about overall safety and traffic-calming plans at an 
upcoming meeting. 3) I support the request that LTA submit a formal request to 
OSTA for Armory to be designated a "No Through Trucks" street.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9a. Commissioner White 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  b. Amanda Pope, 117 London Drive — Hartford Turnpike, Ridge Road, & Robinwood 
Road need a better and safer intersection with a crosswalk to the parks area. I mean 
this whole neighborhood is concerned with outdated sidewalks as you go down state 
street near the Cheese factory. Plus the broken glass there as well as the Whitney 
Lake bridge. Now that my adult/ younger sister is in a wheelchair, I’ve become 
painfully aware of the limited walking/ wheel-chairing zones. When traffic picks up the 
5 different intersecting roads, it is a lot to manage, especially with a dog or kids or a 
disabled person.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9b. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner Zachery seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  c. Cailynn Sweeney, 63 Burke Street — There is excessive speeding on Burke Street. 
Three ideas to reduce excessive speeding: 
 
1. Add 2 STOP signs on Burke Street at the George Street intersection, making the 
intersection a 3-WAY intersection. 
2. Add a speed table to the intersection of Burke Street and George Street. 
3. Add a speed bump at or around 63 Burke Street.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9c. Commissioner Hampton 
seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  d. LaShawn Jefferson, 157 Armory Street — Dear TA: At 3:45 this afternoon, I was 
driving on Prospect Street headed North toward Armory Street to make a right-hand 
turn onto Armory and head East toward Edgehill. I was driving the speed limit (25 
mph) and slowed down considerably to be able to safely make the right-hand turn 
onto Armory (there is no stop sign before the turn). The car behind me was speeding 
and impatient. As I slowed down for the right-hand turn onto Armory, the car behind 
me accelerated to pass me on the left as I began to turn. To pass me, the car behind 
me had to cross the solid yellow line (maybe it is a double line, but the second line is 
quite light) and enter the lane of oncoming traffic (traffic heading South on Prospect). 
The car almost clipped me and almost had a head-on collision with a car coming from 
the opposite direction, heading south on Prospect Street. Of course, this could have 
been avoided if the car behind me was not speeding and had not made the poor 
choice to veer into the opposite lane to pass me before I could turn. But it also could
have been avoided if there were more safety measures in place: a stop sign (and 
crosswalk) on the Southeast corner on Prospect at Armory and another stop sign 
(and crosswalk) on the Northwest corner on Prospect @ Armory. This message 
formally requests additional safety measures at Prospect and Armory, including, but 
not limited to, stop signs and crosswalks.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9d. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  e. LaShawn Jefferson, 157 Armory Street—Traffic along Armory continues to be loud, 
dangerous to residents (and drivers), and voluminous. Commercial trucks using 
Armory as a cut through are now a constant. 
 
1) Is there official, legal residential parking on the North side of Armory Street? If so, 
can the Township paint parking areas on the street? 
2) What is the difference between a speed hump/bump and a speed table? What 
regulation or guidance determines what is installed on any particular street? 
3) This is an official request (again) for speed enforcement along at Armory. What is 
the process of getting a police presence on the street to enforce the speed limit 
(especially during rush hour)? 
4) How does the TA decide where to install speed cameras? This is an official 
request for speed cameras to be installed along Armory Street.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9e. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  f. Eda Bozdemir, 137 Hepburn Road — Please add a crosswalk to this area for safety. 
(Ridge Rd, Hartford Turnpike, and Robinwood Rd)  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9f. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  g. Stephanie Profenna, 29 Myra Road—There’s a huge intersection by the firehouse on 
Hartford Turnpike and Ridge Road. With incoming traffic around the corner, it’s hard 
to cross the street from the dog park or children’s playground towards the firehouse. 
I’m often walking with my baby and dog in tow and don’t always feel safe crossing 
that road.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9g. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  h. Noemi Miranda-Foreman, 274 Augur Street — First Issue — We have been 
experiencing too many cars speeding as well as driving up the wrong way since it is a 
one-way street. There are a lot of children that play out here, and it's extremely 
dangerous when vehicles drive extremely fast. I have a security camera and 
sometimes cars drive so fast the camera barely picks it up. Having speed bumps will 
help control how fast cars are going and also help us be able to get out of our 
driveway safely without being hit by a speeding car. Please get speed bumps to 
control this issue on our street. 
 
Second issue — the way they drew the white line on the left side of the street for 
parking is horrible. They did a solid straight line and people try to cram vehicles in 
without spacing and the line comes across my driveway which people think it's a 
parking spot and always end up blocking my driveway. Is there any way this can be 
changed or if someone can come to draw no parking lines on the left and right side of 
my driveway so that nobody blocks our driveway or even think it's a parking spot.
Last issue, 274 Augur Street — the neighbor to the left of me if you are facing my 
house has a big pick-up truck and he has one of those gardening trailers attached to 
it. He always parks to close to my driveway, and it blocks us from being able to see if 
a car is coming down the street. Is it illegal to have a pick-up truck with a trailer 
attached parked out front that can make it difficult to see when cars are coming 
through?  
  Commissioner White made a motion to transfer item 9h. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  i. Robert B. Cochran, 687 Ridge Road— I would like to petition the city to install a 
crosswalk at this important intersection (Ridge Rd, Hartford Tpke, and Robinwood 
Rd). My wife and infant daughter and I live nearby and frequently cross this busy 
intersection on walks, and being forced to cross without any crosswalk (despite 
several sidewalks leading up to it!) creates a great deal of anxiety and is frankly 
unsafe. Given that the intersection lies in a scenic neighborhood, near a park, and 
along a route regularly used by the New Haven Bike Club, we frequently see other 
walkers, runners, and bicyclists also contending with the same problem.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9i. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  j. Anne Jaroszewicz, 24 Woodlawn Street — Due to the extremely high volume and 
hazardous speed of traffic using Woodlawn Street as a shortcut between Whitney 
and Dixwell Avenues, 42/50 residents (84%) of Woodlawn Street have signed a 
petition for the urgent approval and installation of speed bumps on Woodlawn 
between Whitney Ave and Greenway Street. In addition to the trade parade speeding 
through our street every morning and evening, the school buses are coming through 
at an unconscionable 45 mph. One of Woodlawn's pets was run over by a hit-and-run 
driver last year and residents fear that it's a matter of time before a child on a bicycle 
is hit. THIS HAS TO STOP! For the safety of all Woodlawn Street residents, in 
particular the children, pets and elderly, we call on the Traffic Authority to urgently 
install speed bumps. I am in possession of the signed petition and sent copies of 
these documents to Stephen White and Jim Mesner yesterday. The residents of 
Woodlawn would like to appear before the board as soon as possible.  
  Item 9j. was previously approved at the previous month's meeting (repeat item). 
  k. Mark Weiner, 125 Mill Rock Road— I am writing from my home on Mill Rock Road to 
express great hope that traffic issues on Armory St. can be remediated. My wife and I 
walk on Armory in the morning about four days each week, and I can attest that the 
truck noise has become extreme. I first expressed my views about the need to 
remediate traffic on Armory a city council meeting over twenty years ago. Now the 
issue strikes me as absolutely urgent. As you work to resolve the issue, I am writing 
to express my hope that traffic-calming measures taken on Armory will not simply 
push trucks and other traffic onto Mill Rock Road. I therefore ask that you take Mill 
Rock into consideration in the midst of your efforts to meet the needs of residents on 
Armory. I am confident that you would do so as a matter of course, but for the record, 
I wanted to express my views through this formal channel so that they can be added 
to your overall agenda.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9k. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor.
l. Kayla Bridgemohan, 539 Ridge Road — The intersection needs a crosswalk. Many 
cars have blown through lights and caused accidents at this intersection. Living on 
the corner of Ridge Road, I see it happen all the time. Also, there are many children 
and walking with them and needing to cross that intersection, you can tell from 
experience just how much a crosswalk is needed.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to transfer item 9l. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  m. Miguel Arturo Perez-Cabello, 44 Allene Drive — Stop signs are needed on Corbin 
Road at the corner with Hepburn Road. This corner is within a mile of Ridge Hill 
School. This is a school crossing guard spot. Many people, including children and 
seniors, cross this corner every day. Over the past few months, there have been 
several incidents in which cars traveling on Corbin Road have not stopped, almost 
causing an accident involving pedestrians or other cars. This corner is confusing for 
drivers and pedestrians because there are only two stop signs on Hepburn Road. 
Therefore, cars traveling on Corbin Road tend to drive through this corner without 
yielding. In addition, traffic from west to east on Corbin Road is downhill, which 
motivates drivers to go faster. The solution is simple: two stop signs need to be 
added on Corbin Road to ensure that there are four stop signs at this corner, so 
traffic from all points comes to a stop to prevent accidents involving other cars and 
pedestrians.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to table item 9m. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  n. Hiilei Hobart, 605 Ridge Road— I’m writing to advocate for the installation of a 
crosswalk at the intersection of Ridge Rd and Hartford Turnpike. It would make it so 
much safer for kids.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to transfer item 9n. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  o. Emily DiBenigno,72 Pickwick Road— I wanted to reach out to put in a request to put 
a walkway for pedestrians to safely cross the intersection of Hartford Turnpike and 
Ridge Road right in front of the fire station. I cross this intersection daily, sometimes 
twice a day, to drop my toddler off at daycare. I am not alone in crossing this 
intersection. I see runners, dog walkers, etc. cross daily. This is a very scary 
intersection to cross since it is hard to see cars coming in certain directions.I know 
Hamden is hurting for money, but I would love to see this idea in plans for the future. 
A resolution for this area would be a round-a-about, but to save money, a simple 
crosswalk for pedestrians would help to ensure safety, especially if the cross had its 
own sensor for walkers to cross like they do at the next intersection of Ridge Road 
and Waite Street near the dog park. Thanks for considering! I say "simple cross-walk" 
as I know how much things actually cost... :) I am happy to pitch fundraising for this if 
needed. I am sure Spring Glen and Ridge Hill will have many supportive donors.  
  Commissioner White made a motion to transfer item 9o. to the traffic-calming list. 
Commissioner Ladore seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  p. John Barton, 206 Armory Street — First, and most important, I am hoping we can get 
an update tonight on the traffic-calming project for Armory and surrounding streets 
that has been discussed at prior meetings. We were told that a project was in the 
works, that it needed funding and/or approval at the next South Central Council of 
Government meeting, and that, after that meeting, a hearing would be scheduled for 
public input. I am just looking for an update on what’s happening with that project.
Second, traffic-calming measures are becoming more and more pressing for Armory 
Street. With the start of the Whitney Avenue construction project, there has been a 
marked increase in traffic on Armory Street. Last Friday, I counted 678 vehicles 
passing in front of our house in a two-hour stretch between 7:30am and 9:30am. That 
included 38 dump trucks hauling debris from the Winchester Firearms Building 
demolition project. These trucks can barely make the turn onto Armory, often 
requiring cars to back up at the stop sign. As New Haven has placed speed humps 
on all five of its residential streets that connect Prospect to Whitney, Armory is the 
only residential street that connects those two roads in that area without any traffic-
calming measures. New Haven has also designated Prospect as a “No Thru Truck” 
street, further deterring vehicles from using their residential streets and instead 
driving them onto Armory and Mill Rock. 
 
Finally, I hope the plan for Armory whether through the region or this committee, 
incorporates the following three improvements: (1) speed humps like those on all the 
surrounding residential streets in New Haven; (2) the designation of Armory as a 
“NoThru Truck” street to mirror the same designation that New Haven has placed on 
Prospect Street; and (3) an island at the intersection of Armory and Edgehill to make 
sure traffic slows down through that intersection.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9p. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
  q. Brenda King, 139 Armory Street- TRAFFIC-CALMING Measures Needed on 
ARMORY STREET 
The HUGE INCREASE IN TRAFFIC on Armory Street must be remedied. 
The INCREASING NUMBERS OF DUMP TRUCKS and other trucks must be 
reversed. 
POLICE ENFORCEMENT OF BASIC TRAFFIC LAWS must begin at once on 
Armory Street, as a first step in addressing a problem that is rapidly getting out of 
hand.  
  Commissioner Ladore made a motion to transfer item 9q. to the traffic- calming list. 
Commissioner White seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in favor. 
10. ADJOURNMENT   
 There being no further business to discuss, Commissioner Ladore made a motion to adjourn 
the Traffic Authority regular meeting. Commissioner Zachery seconded the motion. The vote 
was unanimous in favor. The meeting adjourned at 6:14 PM.

  Commissioner Hampton made a motion to move item 5a. to new business for a 
vote. Commissioner Zachery seconded the motion. The vote was unanimous in 
favor. 
  b. Martina Costa, Traffic Safety commendation— I wanted to thank Hamden Traffic 
Authority. My son Jackson is involved in Boy Scouts and he's currently working toward
earning his Traffic Safety merit badge. He's become really interested in learning about 
pedestrian, bicycle, and roadway safety, and during his research online he came across the 
HTA's page on the Hamden website [hamden.com/375/Traffic-Authority]. It was a huge help! 
He found a lot of useful information that helped him better understand traffic safety and safe 
travel practices. He appreciated having such a helpful resource and insisted that we reach out 
to say thank you, so here we are! :) As he's been researching, he's also discovered a number 
of great educational resources. Jackson actually picked one out that he wanted to share with 
you as a way of returning the favor. It's a great guide to pedestrian and bike 
safety:"Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety for All" www.safemotorist.com/pedestrian-and-bicycle-
safety/ It's a wonderful resource for children, parents, and educators, and Jackson thought it
